$comment: What WikiKit actually enforces of cockpit-ui, rule by rule.
COCKPIT-UI.md never names a test. That is why this file exists — and why an
empty `enforced_by` with a real `why` is a truthful entry, not a gap to be
papered over. A style guide that is wrong about itself is worse than none.
The honest summary of this console today: the tokens, the theme, the mount,
the marker, the navigation table and the scope model are TESTS. The rules
that grade what a page looks like were graded by review when the pages were
written, and `bun test` has no layout engine — nothing here holds that a
Tooltip opens, that focus moves, or that four states look different. The
browser check (scripts/check-cockpit-browser.ts) covers three of those and
is not in the gate; the production checklist covers the rest by hand.

CUI-THEME-1.why: Only that the served shell reads the wk-cockpit-theme key. That the store writes the same three values is held by the store's own construction, not by an assertion.

CUI-THEME-2.why: The pre-paint script in index.html and lib/theme-store.ts both treat key-absence as system, but they are edited independently and nothing compares them.

CUI-THEME-3.why: The CSP hash is computed from the served bytes, so a shell without the inline script would ship a policy admitting a script that is not there. That is a proof the script IS in the document — not a proof it runs before paint.

CUI-THEME-5.why: Sign-out reloads and never touches the theme key, which is visible in shell.tsx and covered by hand in scripts/deploy/verify-cockpit-prod.md §2. No test asserts the absence of a write.

CUI-MARK-2.why: data-cockpit-ui is on the SidebarProvider in app/shell.tsx. Reading it would need a rendered tree, and this runner has no DOM.

CUI-PAGE-1.why: A judgement about a page's subject. Graded at review.

CUI-PAGE-2.why: Indirectly: every routed path resolves to exactly one nav entry, and router.tsx names one component export per route.

CUI-ACT-1.why: Sign-in is an anchor and the nav entries are Links, which is the case that mattered most; nothing asserts it, and nothing stops the next page from using a button to navigate.

CUI-ACT-3.why: Graded at review. A lint rule would hold this and does not exist yet.

CUI-ACT-4.why: The consistency test holds the current page-header actions against the retired duplicate empty-state selectors. Broader action hierarchy remains a review judgement.

CUI-ACT-5.why: The Button primitive composes disabled with a spinner rather than swapping its label, so the affordance exists. Whether a page uses it is not checked.

CUI-WORDS-2.why: The consistency test forbids native title attributes and holds the shared tooltip-plus-popover help primitive.

CUI-SEV-2.why: The rule every dashboard breaks, and the one least covered here: nothing asserts that a missing count renders as an em dash rather than 0. Checked by hand in verify-cockpit-prod.md §7.

CUI-LOAD-1.why: DataState and DataTable render skeletons in the shape of the result, so a page using them cannot get this wrong. A page not using them is unchecked.

CUI-LOAD-2.why: ApiError carries the server's words and next_best_actions through to the alert; no test renders one.

CUI-LOAD-3.why: EmptyState requires a title and a description in its type — enforced by the compiler, not by a test.

CUI-LAYOUT-1.why: index.css sets body overflow:hidden and the shell carries min-h-0/min-w-0, which is the mechanism — but only a browser can prove the document does not scroll. scripts/check-cockpit-browser.ts asserts it and is not in the gate.

CUI-LAYOUT-2.why: Graded at review. No lint rule forbids space-y-*.

CUI-LAYOUT-3.why: scripts/check-cockpit-browser.ts rejects every visible table whose scroll width exceeds its container. Not in the gate: it needs a browser, a database and a running server.

CUI-RESP-1.why: scripts/check-cockpit-browser.ts runs every route at 390x844. Same caveat as CUI-LAYOUT-3.

CUI-A11Y-1.why: The vendored Dialog requires a title; no test asserts each call site supplies one.

CUI-A11Y-2.why: Focus behaviour is Radix's, and this runner has no DOM to observe it in.

CUI-A11Y-3.why: Confirm blocks dismissal while its mutation is in flight, in code that has no test around it yet.

CUI-A11Y-4.why: The AST test requires an explicit kebab-case selector on every rendered interactive element outside the vendored UI primitives.

CUI-A11Y-5.why: Aspirational. Badges carry a word beside their tone by construction, but nothing forbids a page from colouring alone.

CUI-AI-1.why: The rule this product needs most: a synthesised claim is not a measurement. STATUS_STATE maps `proposed` to blocked rather than succeeded, which is the mechanism; nothing asserts a page honours it.

CUI-AI-2.why: The console shows no model output directly today — synthesis lands as a change proposal, reviewed as a diff. Revisit when it does.

CUI-AI-3.why: Every claim carries its citation quotes in the page and in the change diff, which IS this rule for this product. Graded at review, not asserted.

CUI-AI-4.why: Indirectly: the changes entry declares the four decision endpoints, and the test proves they exist in ROUTES. An accept/reject affordance without a recording endpoint would fail there.
